issues.body: open_validated calls record_len(dim, degree), whose `8 + dim * 4 + degree * 4` arithmetic is unchecked. Both values are attacker-controlled u32 fields, and wasm32 is explicitly supported, so values such as dim=u32::MAX overflow before the subsequent checked `count.checked_mul(record_len)` guard runs. Depending on build overflow checks this can panic during open or wrap into a bogus record size and invalidate later offset/alignment reasoning. The existing malformed-header test exercises a huge count, but not hostile dim/degree values, so it does not cover this path.
issues.fix_hint: Make record-length construction checked (checked_mul plus checked_add) and return a descriptive Err from open_validated before any wrapped size is used. Add a focused open_from_bytes malformed-header test with u32::MAX dimension and/or degree; ideally exercise the calculation under a 32-bit target or factor it into a usize-width-independent checked helper whose overflow behavior can be tested.
issues.title: Forged graph dimensions overflow record-size arithmetic on wasm32

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes the prior out-of-range PQ-code finding on the real open path and adds non-vacuous mmap and owned-byte regression coverage. However, malformed graph header dimensions still reach unchecked node-record size arithmetic before the checked count/body calculation. On the explicitly supported wasm32 target, a forged u32 dimension or degree can overflow inside record_len (and later produce wrapped offsets or a panic), contradicting the malformed-input fail-cleanly contract. Because this is a new major finding after round 2, progress is regressing under the required scale.
